observations.attempt: Two distinct attacks modeled: (a) does converting a red-listed regression pin from git-diff-based to content-based assertions create a log-omission-through-an-alternate-path (a way for a future PL-12-forbidden change to slip past undetected)? (b) does the mechanical red-pin rehash tool's behavior when pointed at an older ticket's ledger-preserved red.json (the only way to check a red-pinned file with no red.json on this run's own /inline-edit lane) correctly surface — rather than silently swallow — an undeclared change?
evidence: Read the full diff hunk (scripts/sdd-completeness.test.mjs, single hunk, ~lines 1386-1416) directly: it replaces a `git diff --name-only HEAD` ten-path loop (only ever non-empty against a DIRTY local tree — on a clean CI checkout the diff is always empty, so this pin provided ZERO regression protection in CI) with 11 substring/regex content assertions inspecting each file's CURRENT full text. This is a strict widening of what actually gates in CI (previously nothing; now the full merged content is checked on every run), traded for a narrower "must contain the literal token 'inline'" signal — the documented EC-9 residual (a content check cannot notice an edit unrelated to that token) is real but was never this test's job to begin with (per spec's own EC-9 reasoning, itself modeled on an existing, pre-PL-14 precedent already in the same file for docs/PRD_Tickets.md).

Independently spot-checked three of the coordinator-flagged control-plane files against the live tree: `grep -n inline .sdd/bounds.yml scripts/check-lite-eligible.mjs scripts/pipeline-contracts.mjs .sdd/hotfix.md` → zero matches across all four — every content assertion touching these files is currently a true, non-vacuous negative claim, not a check that would pass regardless of content.

Independently re-derived (not merely trusted) review's own adjudication of the red-pin rehash: `node scripts/check-red-integrity.mjs --dir .sdd/ledger/20260809T015417496Z-a537e98a7c24-PR_DELTA-1bf759` (PL-12's preserved run) this session → exit 1, one violation, reporting `scripts/sdd-completeness.test.mjs`'s hash changed (`3f4df8ce…` → `1b11d66b…`) and "changes.json does not declare this change." Traced why: `--dir` (read directly, scripts/check-red-integrity.mjs lines 58-90) points ALL THREE JSON inputs (red.json, spec.json, AND changes.json) at the given directory — so this invocation reads the ledger's FROZEN PL-12 changes.json (which only declares PL-12's own red-test change, `ledger-append.test.mjs` — confirmed by reading that file directly), never the LIVE `.pipeline/changes.json`. Independently read the live `.pipeline/changes.json`'s `redTestChanges` array directly: it names `scripts/sdd-completeness.test.mjs` with an accurate, substantive reason, exactly matching PL-14's actual diff.

This confirms review's account was correct, but also surfaces a real, narrow tooling gap worth naming on its own merits: `check-red-integrity.mjs` has no invocation that mixes an OLD red.json pin (from a red-listed file's originating ticket) with the CURRENT `.pipeline/changes.json` (from a later, unrelated ticket touching that same red-listed file under a lane with no red.json of its own) — this specific cross-ticket scenario always requires a human to manually cross-reference two separate tool outputs, as review did and as this run independently re-did. This is NOT a silent-pass failure mode: every invocation available still exits 1 and forces explicit adjudication (the tool fails closed in both directions — it never silently accepts an undeclared change), so nothing was actually laundered here. It is a usability gap in a rare scenario, not a control gap: no exploit path was demonstrated where this ambiguity causes a real violation to go unflagged.

observations.observation_key: projsayre/sayre|SEC-01|secrets-audit-data-lifecycle|scripts/check-secret-access.mjs's new ALLOWLIST entry for scripts/guard-checker-readonly.test.mjs — mechanically whole-file and permanent, not scoped to the one sanctioned line (PL-13 new surface)|v2-allowlist-whole-file-residual
observations.target_asset: scripts/check-secret-access.mjs's new ALLOWLIST entry for scripts/guard-checker-readonly.test.mjs — mechanically whole-file and permanent, not scoped to the one sanctioned line (PL-13 new surface)
observations.attempt: Modeled the ALLOWLIST entry itself as an alternate credential path outside the designated loader: does exempting scripts/guard-checker-readonly.test.mjs open a route by which a FUTURE edit to that one file could read a genuinely secret-class value from process.env with the gate staying silent forever? Weighed the three mitigants spec.md EC-5 states rather than accepting or dismissing the residual on the ticket's own say-so. Re-confirmed unaffected by PL-14: neither scripts/check-secret-access.mjs nor scripts/guard-checker-readonly.test.mjs is in this diff.
evidence: Read `check-secret-access.mjs`'s scan loop directly (line 1847-1852): `if (!SOURCE_EXTENSION.test(file) || EXCLUDED_SEGMENT.test(file) || ALLOWLIST.has(file)) continue;` — `ALLOWLIST.has(file)` is an exact-string Set membership test with no line/pattern/variable-name scoping. Once a file is a member, EVERY process.env access anywhere in that file, present or future, is silently skipped by this gate for as long as the entry remains — confirmed by reading the loop; there is no per-line or per-identifier suppression mechanism anywhere in this file (matches spec.md EC-5's own "Nothing mechanically narrows an ALLOWLIST entry... today").

Confirmed the CURRENT state of the exempted file does not exploit this today: `git diff HEAD -- scripts/guard-checker-readonly.test.mjs` is empty (byte-unchanged), and its one process.env-touching line (233, `spawnSync(process.execPath, [GUARD], { ..., env: { ...process.env, ...env } })`) reads no secret-class value — it spreads the CURRENT process's own environment into a child process to control TMP/TEMP/TMPDIR for the [C4-mirror] regression tests, confirmed by reading the surrounding test bodies (lines 219-261).

Weighed the three stated mitigants against the actual tree, not merely quoted them: (a) the comment above the entry names the sanctioned access precisely (child-process env spread for TMP/TEMP/TMPDIR injection) — a diff adding an unrelated second env read to this file would visibly contradict that comment at review time, but review is a human/agent process, not a mechanical control; (b) the file has zero production import path (it is a `*.test.mjs` file exercising `scripts/guard-checker-readonly.mjs` as a subprocess) and CI provisions no real credential when it runs; (c) the SIBLING `check-org-secret-access.mjs` gate independently confirmed to still cover this exact file for the Jira raw-column class — its own ALLOWLIST (4 entries, all under services/core/src/db/) does NOT include scripts/guard-checker-readonly.test.mjs, and it scans the same `git ls-files`-derived tracked-file set, so a future edit introducing a `jiraAccessTokenEnc`-class read to this file would still be caught by that gate. Mitigant (c) is real but narrow: it covers only the Jira raw-column class, not AWS/GitHub/JWT/other secret classes.

No time-bounded, named risk-acceptance record (approver/reason/ticket/expiry) exists for this residual anywhere in .pipeline/ or the diff — spec.md's EC-5 discloses it as an "accepted residual" but this is a design note in a spec, not the audit contract's formal risk_acceptance object, so this observation does not treat it as one.

finding.remediation_reference: No per-line/per-pattern suppression mechanism exists in check-secret-access.mjs today (spec.md explicitly rejected adding one as out of scope for this CI-unblock ticket, correctly — a general suppression-comment mechanism is a larger, separate change). A future remediation could either (a) add a narrow, pattern-scoped suppression (e.g. an allowlist keyed to a specific line/pattern hash rather than a whole file, so drift elsewhere in the same file is still caught), or (b) add a lightweight recurring check (e.g. a recorded content-hash or line-count assertion on the ALLOWLISTed file, re-verified in CI) that fails loudly if the file changes at all, forcing a human to re-review the exemption rather than silently inheriting it forever. Not a PL-13 defect — the same whole-file shape already exists for the four pre-existing designated-loader entries and the org-secret-access gate's jiraConnectionStore.rls.test.ts precedent; this is a structural property of the ALLOWLIST mechanism itself, newly extended to a fifth, non-loader file by this ticket.
